title.en: Act I: the prophecy and the plan

hook.en: Act I moves fast: a battle, a prophecy, a reward, a letter and a plan. By its end, a loyal general has agreed to kill his king.

objectives.en: Follow the events of Act I in order
Explain the effect of the prophecies on Macbeth and Banquo
Analyse how Lady Macbeth persuades Macbeth

narration.en: Act I moves fast: a battle, a prophecy, a reward, a letter and a plan. By its end, a loyal general has agreed to kill his king.

body.en: After a bloody battle in which Macbeth and Banquo defeat rebels and invaders, the Witches greet Macbeth as Thane of Glamis (his title), Thane of Cawdor and future king; they tell Banquo that he will father kings, though he will not be one. Moments later, Ross brings news that the king has made Macbeth Thane of Cawdor, as the traitor Cawdor is to be executed. One prophecy has come true, and Macbeth at once begins to think about murder, though the thought frightens him. Banquo warns that evil powers may tell small truths to win our trust and then betray us.

points.en: Witches: Glamis, Cawdor, king; Banquo's line will be kings
Macbeth imagines murder and is afraid
Banquo is wary of the Witches

title.en: On the board: Act I in order

text.en: Act I in order
1. The Witches plan to meet Macbeth
2. A soldier reports Macbeth's courage in battle
3. The prophecies; Macbeth is made Thane of Cawdor
4. Duncan names Malcolm his heir (Prince of Cumberland)
5. Lady Macbeth reads the letter and calls on dark spirits
6. Duncan arrives at Inverness, the Macbeths' castle
7. Macbeth hesitates; his wife persuades him

text.en: Exposition
Battle won; the Witches wait on a heath;
Macbeth is praised as a hero.
Rising action
The prophecies; Cawdor comes true; Macbeth's
first dark thought; Malcolm named heir.
Turning point
Lady Macbeth reads the letter and resolves
that her husband shall be king.
Complication
Duncan arrives as a guest; Macbeth lists
reasons not to act and decides to stop.
Decision
His wife attacks his courage and gives a plan;
Macbeth agrees to the murder.

body.en: Reading Macbeth's letter, Lady Macbeth fears that his nature is too gentle to seize the crown by foul means, and she asks dark spirits to strip her of pity. When Macbeth, after weighing the reasons against murder (Duncan is his king, his kinsman and his guest, and a good ruler), says they will go no further, she attacks his manhood and his love, mocks his fear, and gives a practical plan: drug the guards and blame them. Her strength here contrasts with what happens to her later.

points.en: She calls on spirits to remove her pity
She attacks his courage and offers a plan

explanation.en: The act moves from battle to prophecy, reward, the heir, the letter, the arrival and the decision.

problem.en: How does Shakespeare show Macbeth's inner conflict before the murder? Answer in points.

steps.en: He lists reasons against the murder: duty as subject, kinsman and host, and Duncan's goodness.
He admits that only ambition drives him, and that it may overreach itself.
He tells his wife they will proceed no further.
He gives in only when she questions his manhood and offers a plan, showing his conscience is still alive.

answer.en: Macbeth knows the murder is wrong; his conscience argues against it until his wife's pressure overrules it.
